This behavior closely matches known malicious patterns where Discord bots are used as remote access trojans (RATs) to execute arbitrary commands on infected systems. Although the code does not explicitly steal data like cookies or screenshots, the ability to execute arbitrary shell and JS commands remotely is a critical security risk and a common RAT trait. The code also fetches attachment content over the network and executes it if it matches certain extensions, further increasing risk. The presence of owner checks and permission handling does not mitigate the fundamental risk of remote code execution.
